correctness.rationale: After scaling -6 L_3^(a) to the integral monic cubic and translating X=Y+A, A=a+3>=3, one gets exactly Y³-3AY-2A. An integral root y would satisfy y³=A(3y+2). Odd y gives gcd(y,3y+2)=1, hence 3y+2=±1, uniquely y=-1 with A=1; even y=2k gives 4k³=A(3k+1) with coprime k,3k+1, forcing 3k+1|4 and k∈{-1,0,1}, which produce A=2,0,1. None meets A>=3. Thus every nonnegative integral parameter has irreducible cubic. Discriminant Δ=108A²(A-1)=[6A]²3(a+2)>0 is square exactly when a=3k²-2, k>=1; standard transitive cubic group criterion yields C3 vs S3 and count floor(sqrt((B+2)/3)). Independent SymPy shift/discriminant checks and 100 factorizations corroborated, not a proof of all-a.
residual_risks: Only cubic degree and integer a>=0, no conclusion for negative/fractional parameters or higher degrees.
A bounded computer test does not imply all-parameter irreducibility; that is furnished by integer-divisibility proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for uniform cubic IRREDUCIBILITY for a>=0 and the resulting unconditional group classification, not for the square-discriminant locus itself. Banerjee–Filaseta–Finch–Leidy (2013) explicitly determine cubic square-discriminant parameters but their complete Galois classification in Theorem 2.4 only ranges a<=10. The very recent Das–Dutta–Laishram–Nair arXiv:2610.10614 gives a<=1000 and necessary conditions IF a cubic factor exists; its Theorem 1.2(ii) is not the universal absence proof. Other cited fixed-a large-n and fractional-a results reverse or restrict quantifiers. No actual prior all-a cubic theorem identified, with possible elementary historical derivation retained as risk.
residual_risks: An older elementary root-exclusion proof might exist in difficult-to-index sources.
The discriminant locus alone is NOT new; no priority claimed for it.

value.rationale: Degree three is the first natural cubic case next to the exceptional quadratic Laguerre factor family. Removing the parameter-1000 cutoff solves the entire integer-parameter cubic case and turns a pre-existing square-discriminant parameterization into complete realizable cyclic-versus-symmetric splitting-field classes and exact counting. Its value is a natural uniform classification, not a claim to have rediscovered a discriminant identity.
